title: nail writes the mmseqs target db in parallel
body:
`write_mmseqs_sequence_database` in `mmseqs.rs` writes the mmseqs target db that the prefilter searches. It walks the targets with `Fasta::iter`, which parses each record with `Sequence::from_fasta` from the mapped file. For each record it writes the residues to the db, a line to the db's `.index`, the record's position as its header, and a line to the header `.index`. It runs on one thread, through four files.

The "db write" leaf of the `-s` tree times this writer together with the query db writer, which runs right after it. On the 8-thread run at `92de7c5` (note on nail-1964b2) the leaf took 7.31 s. A run with one Pfam profile against the same 2,455,940 targets took 4.32 s, so the target db is about 4.3 s of it. The rest is the query profile db, nail-811f24.

## Proposal

A rayon loop over ranges of records builds, for each range, the db bytes, the header bytes and each record's lengths. One sequential pass then writes the ranges in order and assigns the offsets for both `.index` files. The db holds only the residues, so the parse can skip the digital bytes and the name that `Sequence::from_fasta` builds. Whether that means a narrower parse here or a cheaper `from_fasta` is part of nail-2ec538.

## Cost

A sequential write of about 470 MB, the size of the db mmseqs built for these targets, should take about 1 s on an SSD. That sets the floor. The estimate is 4.3 s down to 1 or 2 s at 8 threads. Nobody has measured it.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/95b307ba
notes.text: Rewrote the body. The old one described `Database::iter` with a seek and a `read_exact` per record, which `92de7c5` removed. It also counted the whole 15.5 s db write leaf as the target db, when part of the leaf is the query profile db, now nail-811f24.
